lessons.title: Course Material: Checklist (2).pdf
lessons.content:
PAGE_1:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 1 Profitable Pricing –  Cheat Sheet  Introduction ü Price is vitally important ü Small changes can produce dramatic results ü An effective strategy will increase profitability on a long-term basis ü Effective pricing helps you: o Meet/exceed revenue targets o Remain competitive o Retain/Increase market share o Retain customer loyalty o Retain image/reputation  Learning Objectives: ü Define your ideal customer  ü Effectively research your competitors and market trends  ü Position your product or service in your market  ü Understand a variety of pricing strategies and learn which ones work best  ü Create a system for monitoring the results of your pricing  ü Understand when it's good to raise or lower prices

PAGE_2:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 2 Action Steps: Think about some products or services you have bought in the last month or so.  From a pricing perspective, ask yourself: 1. What products or services did you feel were a good value?   2. How long have you been loyal to particular brands that you buy repeatedly from?   3. What differentiates them in terms of their pricing?   4. For products or services that you are willing to pay more for, how does price factor in?

PAGE_3:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 3 Module 1 - Defining Your Customer  ü Create a profile to gain understanding of who your customer is ü It’s not possible to target everyone ü A definition of your ideal customer will help you: o Tailor marketing o Boost appeal o Brand your company o Set prices accordingly o Fashion strategies ü Targeting cuts down on unnecessary costs ü Defining your target does not mean you are leaving anyone out  Creating Your Customer Profile ü Be as specific as possible about who your target customer is ü Create a full profile of your ideal customer, like a specific individual ü Demographic information includes: o Age o Geographic location o Gender o Income level o Education level o Marital status o Family composition o Occupation

PAGE_4:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 4 ü Psychographic information includes: o Personality o Attitudes o Values o Hobbies o Lifestyle o Behavior o How they see themselves  ü Buying behavior information includes: o Where? o When? o Strategy o Emotions o Price  Where to Find Customer Data ü You can never have too much data about your customers  Current customers ü Gather information about them through: o Surveys o Sales follow-ups o Social media interaction o Other touch points

PAGE_5:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 5 Your Competitors’ customers ü Start with whatever customer data you have on file ü Ask for information directly  Your products and services ü Ask yourself what type of person would benefit ü Once you’ve narrowed down your target market ask yourself: o Are there enough people? o Could some points be made more specific? o Will they really benefit? o What drives their decisions? o Can they afford it? o Can I reach them with my value message?  Examples of Target Market Profiles ü An insufficient customer profile doesn’t tell you much, except that the customer needs your product ü A sufficient one makes it easy to understand the value your product holds to the customer   Action Steps: 1. Create a profile of your existing and ideal customer types. If you do not have access to your customer information, consider surveying them.  2. For both your existing and ideal customer base, consider demographic information, psychographics, and buying strategies.  3. Does your existing customer type align with your ideal customer type?

PAGE_6:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 6 Module 2 - Know Your Competitors  ü You need to understand the competitive landscape to position and price accordingly ü Take advantage of their weaknesses  Finding Your Competitors ü Keep an eye out for new competitors ü The competitive landscape is always changing ü Places to look for existing competitors include o Local business directories o Local Chamber of Commerce o Advertisements o Press reports o Exhibitions and trade fairs o Surveys and questionnaires o Internet searches o Customer information o Flyer, brochures and other literature o Products/Services similar to yours o Existing clients ü Make a list and identify those competitors who are competing for the same customer base

PAGE_7:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 7 What to Research ü Nearly any information about your competitors can be helpful ü Here are questions to ask: o How do they market? o What are their prices like? o What is their unique value? o How do they innovate? o How big are they? o What is their employee caliber? o Who owns the business? o Where in the media can you find them? o What kind of web presence do they have? o What is their reputation like? o How do they distribute? o What special services do they offer? o Get a copy of their annual report o What do customers see as their strengths and weaknesses? o What is their customer loyalty like? o Has there been an influx or decrease of customers? o What new products are they developing? o What financial resources do they have?

PAGE_8:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 8 Gathering Information on Potential Competitors ü Pay attention to trends to help predict what future competitors you’ll need to consider ü Places to look for potential competitor information include: o Industry blogs o Email newsletters o Social media trends o Trade shows and conferences o Customer dialogue   Action Steps: 1. Perform research about your competitors.  Use the Competitor Research Questions document to help guide your research and use the Know Your Competitors spreadsheet to summarize and keep track of multiple competitors. 2. What trends are impacting your business?

PAGE_9:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 9 Module 3 - Positioning Your Product or Service  ü Create an image of your company and its products/services in the minds of customers  Value vs Price ü Value is use someone gets out of a product ü It exists in the end-user’s mind ü Value is subjective ü Price refers to the actual amount paid ü The price doesn’t always reflect something tangible ü Positioning shows value and highlights what’s unique  Adding Value ü Add value to your product or service to make it easier to position ü Things that add value include: o Speeding up service/delivery o Taking extra care in quality o Make your company more reliable or trustworthy o Improve customer service o Incorporate new technology o Make the purchasing process easier ü Small extra things add value to your offering

PAGE_10:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 10 Your Positioning Statement ü The way you position affects what comes to a customer’s mind when they think of you ü Positioning should emphasize value you offer and what makes your product unique ü Your positioning should include this information: o For o Who o Brand is o That o Because o So that o Best expressed by ü Good positioning is: o Single-minded o Meaningful o Focused on outcome o Unique o Important o Sustainable o Believable o True  Examples of Positioning Statements ü Keep in mind the specific meaning and value to your market ü Examples of brands with great positioning include: o BMW o Fed Ex

PAGE_11:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 11 o 7-Up o Miller Lite o Subway o Duracell o U.S. Army o Apple Computer   Action Steps: 1. Define what value your product or service offers 2. Create a positioning statement using this model:   Ø For: Target market (demographically) Ø Who: Target market (psychographically) Ø Brand is: Type of business you’re in Ø That: Functional benefit or value your product or service offers Ø Because: Proof points (no more than three) Ø So that: Emotional benefit Ø Best expressed by: Tagline

PAGE_12:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 12 Module 4 - How to Create a Pricing Strategy  ü There are several pricing models commonly used to determine price ü Each starts at a different point of the commodity exchange  Cost-Plus Pricing ü Cost refers to the amount spent to produce product/service ü Consider what goes into a product such as: o Raw materials o Labor o Instruments of labor o Externalities/Overhead costs ü Two types of costs – fixed and variable o Variable costs will change so make allowance  Value-Based Pricing ü Has the potential to bring great profits but it’s the hardest to gauge ü Charge what customers are willing to pay ü All pricing is value-based to an extent ü Difference is in the flexibility ü Gather exhaustive information to find out what customers are willing to pay ü Involves some psychological tricks

PAGE_13:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 13 Competitor-Based Pricing ü Analysis of competitors and market conditions ü Appropriate pricing ü Methods include: o Undercut competitors o Price higher and offer more value  Service-Based Pricing ü Charge hourly or by project ü Hourly rate can ensure costs are covered ü Some purchasers find it hard to budget for services ü Project rates are easier for the customer but more complicated for the provider  Revenue Targets and Profit Margins ü Two techniques for pricing products are setting revenue targets and profit margins ü Decide how much you want your business to earn and work backwards  Pricing Tactics ü Which strategy you rely on will depend on the type of product and tastes of your target market ü There are pricing tactics that can be used to influence buyer behaviour and sales  Discounting ü Offering reduced prices can drive sales ü Constant discounting can backfire

PAGE_14:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 14 Freemiums ü Common for digital products ü Offer a free version and a premium version  Bundling ü Selling a package of goods or services together at a lower price  High-Low pricing ü Position as higher quality or higher value than competitors and charge more  Decoy ü Offer a handful of similar products at different price points ü One is the “decoy”  Odd value pricing ü Companies choose an o
